model_agnostic_meta_learning.summary: Meta-trains a starting policy so that a few gradient steps on the latest realised bars adapt it to the current regime, then adapts it that way for every block of the test walk.
model_agnostic_meta_learning.implementationNote: Bridge: tasks are blocks of the training span; the start policy is meta-trained (second order) so a few steps on a block's realised context maximise that block's tape reward. P(up) = the adapted policy's long share of long + short. Differs from the spec: adaptation reads only rewards already realised at the bar, once per block. Expect: a gain only where regimes outlast a block.

native.produces: A set of starting weights chosen so that a few plain gradient steps on a small support set of a new task turn them into a model that performs well on that task.
native.targetVariable: The loss of the adapted model on a task's query set, which for a trading policy is the reward it collects on a block of bars after adapting on the outcomes known just before that block.
native.objectiveNote: The outer loss is taken after the inner gradient steps and differentiated back through them to the shared start, and in this repository the tasks are time blocks of the training span, each with the recently realised bars before it as support set and the block itself as query set.

metrics.why: The whole claim of the method is that a few inner gradient steps on the support set help, so the native test is the reward on a later block from the weights after those steps compared with the reward on the same block from the shared start left untouched.
metrics.baseline: The same meta-learned starting weights on the same later block with the inner steps skipped.

metrics.why: The starting weights are trained for what happens after the inner steps, so the fair headline is the reward that the preferred action of the adapted policy earns on test blocks whose support sets were never part of the outer loop.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape collects.

metrics.why: The method is agnostic to the model, and its regression form adapts a forecast head with the same inner steps, so the absolute-error skill of that adapted forecast against forecasting no move tests the adaptation on a target with no trading rule in it.
metrics.baseline: The no-change forecast on the same resolved bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The order in which task batches reach the outer loop and the draw of the starting weights both depend on the seed, and second-order gradients are high in variance, so the spread of the adapted reward across seeds bounds how much one run means.
metrics.baseline: The same model on the same series with only the seed changed.

metrics.why: The exact outer update differentiates through the inner gradient steps, which can produce very large gradients, so the size of the outer gradient per step shows when the first-order shortcut or clipping is needed.

An inner step that is too large on a small support set can throw the adapted policy onto a single action for a whole block, and the entropy of the adapted action shares exposes that before the reward does.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of three, the entropy of a policy that weighs short, flat and long equally.

metrics.why: The kept starting weights are those of the epoch whose adapted policy earned most on the validation span, so that reward is optimistic by the choosing and is read only next to the test value.
metrics.baseline: The reward of the same kept starting weights, adapted the same way, on the fold's test tape.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The outer objective is the query loss after adaptation and carries no risk term, so a return per unit of risk belongs to the as-run layer only.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: The inner and outer losses treat gains and losses alike, so a ratio built on losing bars describes the engine's trading rule and costs.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: Each task is scored as a set of separate decisions and no equity path is ever formed, so a peak-to-trough fall is measured only as run.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: The method produces adapted weights and per-bar preferences, and closed trades come from the engine's holding rule.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: Position sizing is a money-management rule and not a measurement, and nothing in the support and query split estimates a bet size.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: In the reward-trained form the adapted network outputs action preferences and not the odds of an up bar, so a logarithmic score would grade a number that was never meant as a forecast probability.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter implements the bi-level loop of the specification, with plain inner gradient steps on a support set and a second-order outer update of the shared start, but its tasks are time blocks of one instrument, the support set of a block is the stretch of bars before it whose outcomes are already known at the block's first bar, the adaptation is done once per block and reused for every bar in it, and the environment is a fixed reward tape in which the market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure the direction calls of a policy re-tuned on recent realised rewards.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each block of bars the meta-learned starting weights take their inner gradient steps on the realised rewards of the bars just before the block, the adapted policy gives softmax shares for short, flat and long, and the probability of up is the long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows the negative of the adapted policy's expected tape reward plus its entropy bonus on each block after the inner steps, in move-scale reward units and averaged over task batches; on validation rows nats of the adapted long share

meaningful.why: The starting weights are trained so that the policy earns reward after costs once it has taken its inner steps on recent realised bars, so the money made by trading the adapted policy's preferred side is the as-run number closest to that aim, read against buy and hold on the same folds.
It shows how steadily the calls of the block-by-block adapted policy earned per bar after costs, which tells whether re-tuning on recent rewards tracked the market or chased the last block's noise.
Inner steps on a context of rising bars push the adapted policy toward long, and subtracting buy and hold on the same folds shows what the adaptation earned beyond following the recent drift.

Each block's policy is adapted on what the previous stretch paid, so a regime that reverses inside a block is traded with stale weights, and the deepest hole on the marked-to-market path shows what that lag cost.
It compares what the winning trades opened by the adapted policy's preferred side made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count.
It counts how many trades opened when the adapted policy changed side closed in profit, which describes the result's shape while the engine's holding rule decides when each trade ends.
It counts how often the adapted long share crossed the short share, which can happen at a block boundary purely because the weights were re-adapted, and every trading number is read with it.

The policy's weights change at the start of every adaptation block, which can flip its preferred side with no change in the market, and this turnover shows how much of the result those flips handed to costs.
It shows how often the adapted policy preferred long to short, which exposes inner steps that simply copy the direction of the most recent realised bars.

The hard call is up whenever the adapted long share is at least the short share, so the hit rate tests whether the side the inner steps moved the policy toward is also the side price went, against calling the fold's training majority direction.
Averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether the adapted policy still reads the features inside a block or was pushed onto one side for the whole block by its support set.
It states in one symmetric number whether the adapted policy's preferred side moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the inner steps added nothing beyond a lean.
The adapted long share is a continuous number, but its scale shifts with every block's re-adaptation, so this ranking across blocks shows only loosely whether stronger long leanings go with up bars.

The price line comes from a second network of the same kind, meta-trained with a Huber loss and adapted on the realised moves before each block, so this tests whether that separately adapted forecast beats forecasting no move.
It gives in points the typical miss of the separately meta-trained and block-adapted forecast network, read beside the miss of the no-change forecast on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the adapted forecast network, which is trained on the move with no costs and is a different network from the policy, so it can disagree with the traded side.
Inner steps on the realised moves of a trending context tilt the adapted forecast network in the trend's direction, and the mean signed miss shows whether its skill is only that tilt.

The kept starting weights are those of the epoch whose adapted action shares earned the highest mean net reward on the validation span, so this reward is optimistic and is shown only beside the test result.

It is the selection score that chose the hidden size, the outer and inner learning rates, the inner step count and the entropy coefficient on training blocks, flattered by that choosing and shown only beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The adapted long share is a preference shaped by reward, costs and the entropy bonus and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as forecast odds says nothing about the adaptation.
It grades the adapted policy's long share as if it were a probability of an up bar, which neither the inner steps nor the outer loss asked it to be.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the adapted action shares were never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the inner step size and the entropy bonus, not an over-confident or timid forecaster.
It is built on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, so neither half refers to anything the policy stated.

The training curve holds the negative expected tape reward of the adapted policy with its entropy bonus while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two different quantities.

With the long-only setting off and no stop or target the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share reflects the engine overriding the policy's flat action and not how often the policy wanted a position.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The engine overrides the agent's own flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is long whenever the adapted long share is at least the short share, even on bars where flat was the most preferred action.

Tasks are time blocks of one instrument, and the test-time inner steps read only rewards already realised at the block's first bar, once per block, so the policy inside a block does not react to what happens during that block.
A block with too few realised context rows is scored with the starting weights unadapted.
The price line is a second network meta-trained separately on the scaled move and kept on its validation Huber loss, so it is not the policy and its sign can differ from the traded call.

The kept epoch of the direction model is the one whose adapted action shares, flat included, earned the highest mean net reward on the validation span, which is not the quantity the trading metrics score.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because each label spans the label horizon, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is the Micro Nasdaq account figure, a stated assumption.

reptile_meta_learning.summary: First-order meta-learning: repeatedly fine-tunes a copy of the policy on one block of bars and moves the shared starting weights part of the way toward it; the test walk fine-tunes the same way on the latest realised bars.
reptile_meta_learning.implementationNote: Bridge: each block of the training span is a task; K SGD steps on it, then the start weights move toward the result (step annealed). P(up) = the adapted policy's long share of long + short. Differs from the spec: adaptation reads only rewards already realised at the bar, once per block; the market ignores the agent. Expect: close to the plain policy when regimes are short.

native.produces: A shared set of starting weights for a policy network, built so that a few ordinary gradient steps on a new task's own data turn it into a policy fitted to that task, which then gives a trading action for each bar.
native.targetVariable: The reward a task-adapted policy collects on a task after a few fine-tuning steps from the shared starting weights, where a task is one instrument or one stretch of market history.
native.objectiveNote: Reptile never differentiates through the fine-tuning steps: it clones the starting weights, runs several plain gradient steps on one task, and moves the starting weights a fraction of the way toward where those steps ended, so the displacement stands in for the meta-gradient; in the Model Cycle the tasks are time blocks of one instrument's training span and not separate instruments.

metrics.why: Reptile's whole claim is that its starting weights fine-tune well in a few inner steps, so the fair test is the reward on a later block after those inner steps minus the reward of the same starting weights used on that block with the inner steps skipped.
metrics.baseline: The same meta-trained starting weights applied to the same later block with zero inner steps.

metrics.why: After the inner steps the fine-tuned copy is a policy over short, flat and long, and this is the reward per decision that copy's own preferred action earns on bars that came after everything the starting weights and the inner steps were allowed to read.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape pays.

metrics.why: The starting weights are moved toward one randomly ordered batch of tasks at a time, so two runs that differ only in seed visit the blocks in a different order and can settle on different starting points, and this spread shows how much of the result is that ordering.
metrics.baseline: The spread of the same Reptile learner's test reward across reruns on the same series that differ only in seed.

metrics.why: The inner-loop loss at the last fine-tuning step of each block, followed across outer updates while the outer step size is annealed toward zero, shows whether the starting weights are settling or still being dragged from block to block.
metrics.baseline: The same inner-loop loss at the first outer update of the same run.

metrics.why: A few large inner steps on one block can push the softmax over short, flat and long onto a single action, and the entropy of the fine-tuned copy shows whether fine-tuning left any spread in the policy or collapsed it.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of the number of actions, which is the entropy of a policy with no preference.

metrics.why: The kept starting weights are the ones whose fine-tuned copies earned the most on the validation stretch, so this number is flattered by that choice and is shown only beside the reward the same weights earn on the test stretch.
metrics.baseline: The same learner's mean reward per decision on the test tape of the same fold.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: Reptile natively produces starting weights and a fine-tuned policy, and a Sharpe ratio grades the engine's trading rule and costs applied to that policy's call, so it is reported as run only and the pass mark printed beside it was invented by the generator.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: A downside-risk ratio needs an equity path, which only appears when the Model Cycle trades the fine-tuned copy's direction call with costs, so it belongs to the as-run layer and not to the displacement update itself.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: Drawdown is a property of the money path produced by the engine's position rule, and the Reptile update is rewarded one decision at a time with no account balance in its state, so the drawdown is an as-run number only.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: Winning and losing trades are created by the engine opening and closing positions when the fine-tuned copy's call flips, which the Reptile specification does not define, so the ratio is an as-run number only.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: Reptile's policy picks short, flat or long and never outputs a fraction of capital, and the Model Cycle trades a fixed number of contracts, so a sizing fraction was stamped on by the generator and nothing in this model produces it.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The fine-tuned copy outputs how strongly it prefers each action under a reward that includes costs, which is a preference and not a statement of how often price rises, so grading it as forecast odds grades something Reptile never stated.

notApplicable.name: Value overestimation gap
notApplicable.why: The Reptile learner described here carries no critic or action-value estimate, only a policy network whose weights are displaced, so there is no predicted value to compare with the realised return.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The specification defines a way to find starting weights and names no position sizing, fill rule or cost, so a return per unit of risk only exists once the Model Cycle trades the fine-tuned copy's call.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter implements the Reptile update itself, with plain gradient steps on one task, a displacement of the starting weights toward the result averaged over a meta-batch, and an outer step size annealed across epochs, but the tasks are time blocks of one instrument's training span and not separate instruments, each test block is fine-tuned once on the earlier bars whose outcome is already known at the block's first bar, and the environment is a fixed reward tape: the market does not react to the agent and its position is not in the state, so the as-run numbers measure cost-aware reward-weighted direction calls of a small feed-forward policy that is re-tuned block by block.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each block of adaptation interval bars the meta-learned starting weights take the inner steps on the realised context rows before the block, the fine-tuned network gives softmax shares for short, flat and long from the bar's feature row, and the probability of up is the long share divided by the sum of the long and short shares, with the flat share discarded and nothing fitted to outcomes.

stepQuantity.unit: on training rows minus the sum of the policy-share-weighted reward and the entropy bonus, taken at the last inner step of each block and averaged over a meta-batch, in move-scale reward units; on validation rows nats of the long share

meaningful.why: It is the money made by going long whenever the block-adapted policy's long share is at least its short share and short otherwise, under the engine's fill rule and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds.

It measures how steadily the sign of the fine-tuned policy's preference earned money per bar after costs, and it is also what the hyperparameter search steered the inner learning rate, inner step count and outer step size toward on training blocks.

It divides the average bar's net by the root mean square of only the losing bars, taken over all bars, while following the block-adapted policy's long-versus-short call, so it separates a call whose losses are small from one whose gains are merely steady, and a regime change inside a block traded with weights tuned to the earlier bars shows up here as a cluster of losing bars.

It shows the deepest hole dug while following the adapted call, which matters here because each block is re-tuned on the bars just before it and a change of regime inside a block is traded with weights tuned to the old one.

It compares what the winning trades opened by the adapted policy's call made with what the losing ones gave back after costs, read with the trade count beside it because the call can stay on one side for a whole block.
It counts how many trades opened when the adapted call flipped ended in profit after costs, which describes the shape of the results of trading this policy and is not a direction hit rate.

A position is kept while the fine-tuned policy's long share stays on one side of its short share, so this counts flips of that preference, including flips caused by the weights being re-tuned at a block boundary.
The weights change at every block boundary, and this turnover figure shows whether those re-tunings make the call flip so often that costs eat the reward the inner steps were chasing.
Fine-tuning on a short context that happened to trend can tilt the whole block long or short, and this share of up calls exposes a policy that is in effect following the recent drift.

The hard call is up whenever the adapted policy's long share is at least its short share, so the hit rate tests that preference line against calling every bar the fold's training majority direction, keeping in mind the policy was trained on reward net of costs and not on hits.
A block tuned on a drifting context can call one direction throughout, and averaging the hit rate on up bars and on down bars shows whether the fine-tuned copy does more than follow that drift.

It sums up in one symmetric number whether the side the fine-tuned policy prefers moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the inner steps on past rewards added nothing about the bars that followed.

The long share is a continuous preference, so this shows whether bars the adapted policy leaned long on harder went up more often, with the warning that the scale of the share shifts at every block boundary when the weights are re-tuned.

The forecast line comes from a second Reptile learner with a single regression output, meta-trained on the Huber loss of the scaled move and fine-tuned block by block on realised moves, so this tests that second network against forecasting no move and says nothing about the traded call.
It gives in points the typical miss of the block-adapted regression network's forecast of the horizon move, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars.
It checks the sign of the regression learner's forecast, which comes from different weights and a different loss from the policy that makes the traded call, so the two can disagree on the same bar.

It is the selection score that chose the hidden size, inner learning rate, inner step count, outer step size and entropy coefficient on training blocks, flattered by that choosing and shown only beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The long share is a preference shaped by reward net of costs and by the entropy bonus and was never fitted to how often price rises, so scoring it as forecast odds grades something the adapted policy did not state.

It grades the long share as if it were a probability of an up bar, while the inner steps and the displacement update only chase reward, so a good or bad value says nothing about the policy's decisions.
Calibration compares stated odds with observed frequencies, and the fine-tuned policy's action shares were never meant to equal the frequency of up bars.
The slope of outcomes on the log-odds of the long share reads the strength of the entropy bonus and how far the inner steps pushed the weights, not an over-confident or timid forecast.
It is built on the Brier score of a preference share and on a hindsight up share of the test bars, so neither half refers to anything the adapted policy stated.

The training curve holds minus the policy-weighted reward with its entropy bonus at the last inner step, while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the long share, so their difference compares two different quantities.

With the long-only setting off the engine never goes flat once in a trade, so this share reflects the engine overriding the policy's flat action and not how often the adapted policy wanted a position.

caveats: The market does not react to the agent and the agent's position is not in the state, so each decision is rewarded as one fixed trade over the label horizon and nothing in training resembles managing an open position.

The tasks are time blocks of adaptation interval bars cut from one instrument's training span, so the starting weights learn to re-tune from one stretch of this series to the next and not from one instrument to another.

During meta-training the inner steps run on a block's own rows, but on validation and test bars they run on the context rows before the block whose outcome is already known there, so the model is used in a slightly different way from the way it was trained.
Every bar of a block shares one adaptation made at the block's first bar, and a block with fewer realised context rows than the adapter's minimum is scored with the starting weights unchanged.

The engine overrides the policy's own flat action, its sizing and its holding period: the traded side is long whenever the long share is at least the short share, even on bars where flat was the most preferred action.

The kept epoch of the direction model is the one whose fine-tuned copies earned the highest policy-share-weighted reward on the validation rows, valued close to close less one round trip with flat included, which is not the long-versus-short rule the engine then trades.

The price forecast comes from a separately meta-trained regression network whose kept epoch is chosen on its validation Huber loss, so the forecast line and the traded call do not come from the same weights.
Consecutive decisions share future bars because each reward spans the label horizon, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The trading numbers follow the run's own long-only, holding bars, stop loss ticks, take profit ticks and contracts settings, the last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's figure applied as a stated assumption.

reinforcement_learning_squared.summary: A recurrent policy that reads each bar together with its own earlier positions and the rewards they realised, so the learning happens inside its hidden state as the window unfolds.
reinforcement_learning_squared.implementationNote: Bridge: a GRU reads each bar of a fixed window with its own position h bars earlier and the reward that position has realised by now. P(up) = the last step's long share of long + short. Differs from the spec: trained by the exact expected-reward gradient (the tape prices every action) instead of PPO, and the hidden state restarts every window. Expect: close to a plain recurrent policy.

native.produces: A recurrent policy whose hidden state, fed with the previous action and the reward it earned alongside the current state, carries out the adaptation to a new task as it runs forward through a trial.
native.targetVariable: The total reward collected across a whole trial of several episodes on one task, with the hidden state kept running from the first step to the last.
native.objectiveNote: There is no inner gradient step: the slow outer loop trains the recurrent weights on whole-trial return so that the fast adaptation happens inside the hidden state as it reads its own earlier actions and rewards, and in this repository a trial is one window of consecutive bars, so the tasks are time blocks.

metrics.why: Adaptation here is the hidden state filling up with evidence about how the policy's own recent actions paid, so the native test is the reward late in a trial, once that evidence has been read, compared with the reward of the same policy at the start of the trial with an empty hidden state.
metrics.baseline: The same recurrent policy on the same bars with its hidden state freshly reset and no action or reward history read.

metrics.why: The outer loop trains for trial-level reward, so the headline is the reward of the action preferred by the recurrent policy at the end of each window on test bars, where the hidden state has only that window's own history to learn from.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape collects.

metrics.why: Blanking the previous-action and previous-reward inputs leaves an ordinary recurrent policy that sees only the market, and the reward it loses compared with the full model is what the fed-back history contributed.
metrics.baseline: The same recurrent policy with its previous-action and previous-reward inputs set to zero, on the same folds.

metrics.why: In the specification a value head shares the hidden state and supplies the advantage over the whole trial, so the share of trial return it explains shows whether the outer policy-gradient update is learning from signal.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value of a head that predicts the same return at every step.

metrics.why: Credit must travel back across a whole trial through the recurrence, which is unstable, and the entropy of the action shares per step shows whether the policy settled on one action before the hidden state had anything to adapt to.
metrics.baseline: The natural logarithm of three, the entropy of a policy that weighs short, flat and long equally.

metrics.why: The recurrent weights start from a seeded draw and the windows reach the outer loop in a seeded order, so the spread of trial reward across seeds says whether the learned adaptation rule is repeatable.
metrics.baseline: The same model on the same series with only the seed changed.

metrics.why: The kept recurrent weights are those of the epoch with the best validation reward at the last step of each window, so that reward is flattered by the choosing and belongs beside the test value only.
metrics.baseline: The reward of the same kept recurrent policy on the fold's test tape.

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The outer objective is the summed reward of a trial with no risk term, so a return per unit of risk belongs to the as-run layer only.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio

native.objectiveNote: The temporal-difference error is taken on the whole vector of basis outcomes at once instead of on a single reward, and a second small least-squares fit of rewards on basis outcomes recovers the weights whenever the goal changes, after which the action is the best one across the whole library of policies.

metrics.why: The whole point of splitting value into slow outcome tables and quick reward weights is that refitting only the weights on a small fresh sample earns more on the next block than keeping the weights fitted earlier.
metrics.baseline: The same outcome tables and policy library acting on the same later block with the reward weights left at their earlier fit.

metrics.why: After the weights are refitted the agent takes the action with the highest value across the library, and the reward that action collects on a later block is what the transfer was for.
metrics.baseline: Zero reward per decision, which is what staying flat on every bar of the same tape pays.

metrics.baseline: The best single policy of the same library on the same block, valued with the same refitted weights.

metrics.why: The transfer is valid only while reward is a weighted sum of the basis outcomes, and the specification names the leftover of the weight refit as the place where a reward that breaks this assumption shows itself.
metrics.baseline: One, the value when the basis outcomes explain none of the reward.

metrics.why: The action value is a maximum over the library of table-times-weight products, and a maximum over noisy estimates leans high, so the promised value of the chosen action is compared with the discounted reward that followed it.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value when the promised action value matches the reward that followed.

metrics.why: If the refitted weights make one library policy win on nearly every bar, the agent has become always long, always short or always flat, and the split of bars between the three positions shows it at once.
